When /proc/sys/kernel/ftrace_enabled is set to zero
tracing is disabled. But the records that represent the functions
still hold information about the ftrace_ops that are hooked to them.
ftrace_ops may request ""REGS"" (have a full set of pt_regs passed to
the callback)
column2: or ""TRAMP"" (the ops has its own trampoline to use).

column1: When the record is updated to represent the state of the ops hooked
to it
column2: it sets ""REGS_EN"" and/or ""TRAMP_EN"" to state that the callback

column1: points to the correct trampoline (REGS has its own trampoline).
When ftrace_enabled is set to zero
column2: all ftrace locations are a nop

column1: so they do not point to any trampoline. But the _EN flags are still
set. This can cause the accounting to go wrong when ftrace_enabled
is cleared and an ops that has a trampoline is registered or unregistered.
For example
column2: the following will cause ftrace to crash:

column1: # echo function_graph > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/current_tracer
# echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/ftrace_enabled
# echo nop > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/current_tracer
# echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/ftrace_enabled
# echo function_graph > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/current_tracer
As function_graph uses a trampoline
column2: when ftrace_enabled is set to zero

column1: the updates to the record are not done. When enabling function_graph
again
column2: the record will still have the TRAMP_EN flag set

column1: look for an op that has a trampoline other than the function_graph
ops
